key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld-pool simulation, AI surrogates and robot simulation to screen in-space welding conditions and control strategies before physical testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could help robotic welding systems adjust power as travel speed changes, supporting future on-orbit construction and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model with phase change, effective thermocapillary transport and local pressure; gravity assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates evaluated by repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis UR5 welding with proportional power control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation remain necessary.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
